title: The liquid in the pod
fact: Most e-liquid nicotine is extracted from tobacco waste in India. Harvesters absorb the same nicotine through their skin from wet leaves: 'green tobacco sickness'.
note: The study is about tobacco farms in India. Not every e-liquid uses Indian tobacco.
credit: My own pod: the mouthpiece on top, the liquid in the tank, the coil inside. Photo by me, 12 October 2026.

title: The coil you breathe through
fact: The hot coil is where the metal comes from: in 56 users' devices, 57% of aerosol samples exceeded the safe inhalation limit for nickel and 68% for chromium.
note: Measured in 56 devices in one US study. Levels differ between brands.
credit: The coil and its two wires at the end of the pod. Real part. Photo cut from Raimond Spekking, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Not a cigarette, a small electronic product
fact: One vape weighs about 50 grams, and plastic can be up to about 80% of it. It is not a normal cigarette; it is a small electronic product. Would you use a phone for three days and then throw it away?
note: Average weight and plastic share from the study, not this exact model.
credit: The plastic shell, cut open. Real part from another disposable. Photo cut from wiki.recessim.com, CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: A two-year battery, used for three days
fact: After more than 700 charging cycles the battery still keeps over 90% of its capacity. The lithium inside the vapes bought in one year could power nearly 5,000 electric cars. A battery that could be used for two years is thrown away with a single-use vape after three days. Why do we only let it live for three days?
note: 700 cycles was tested in a lab. The car number is an estimate for one year of UK sales.
credit: The lithium battery, 3.7 V 1.85 Wh. Real part. Photo cut from Raimond Spekking, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Made in Shajing, Shenzhen
fact: About 85.7% of the world's vaping devices are made in Shajing, Shenzhen, and about 500,000 people worked in the factories around Shenzhen. China produces the e-cigarettes for the whole world, but bans them at home. So when you smoke one for three days, whose three days are behind it?
note: Numbers are from 2020 reporting. The number of workers changes every year.
